releases.name: Patch: ABORT backlog and fidelity fixes
releases.summary:
Ship 0.4.1: a patch release closing the open items the v0.4.0 ABORT review recorded, and two of the five fidelity problems it accepted. Continuous integration now runs the gates that were hand-run — it found a Linux-only defect on its first run — and the vendored bundles carry verified digests. Asset loading is bounded by file type as well as directory, so files beside a document are no longer readable on render; saving refuses to clobber a change made on disk, preserves extended attributes and refuses a read-only target; and a bounded event trail with build identity means a reported failure can be root-caused. Inline
is no longer deleted and CRLF line endings survive an edit. The accepted GA blocker remains open and is now scoped from measurement rather than from review findings: it is five problems, not one, and inline HTML was never the cause. See docs/decisions/2026-08-08-markdown-fidelity-scope.md.

releases.name: Fidelity repair and domain ownership
releases.summary: Ship 0.5.0. The reason to release is a data-corruption defect: a GFM footnote definition was collected as a link reference definition, so restoration appended a copy of something never lost — and the copy was re-collected on the next pass. Files grew by one definition per save, without bound. It shipped in 0.4.1, survived review, and was found by surveying 49 ordinary constructs rather than by the corpus. Four more constructs now round-trip (closing ATX hashes, repeated ordered markers, tab-separated bullets, trailing newline), taking byte-identical round trips from 35 of 49 to 38 of 49; nothing is deleted any more, only respelled. Preserving the document's own trailing newline also fixed a bug that looked unrelated: a list-first document was marked modified the moment it opened. Every frontend failure surface now records into the event trail rather than a console no production build can display, including a refused link scheme — an autonomous security decision that previously left no trace at all. Five risk records that described a codebase which no longer existed were reconciled against the source. The editor adapter, the DOM shell and the Wails binding surface each gave up the domain logic they were carrying, to a fidelity registry, six markdown modules and internal/session.

releases.name: Finder arrival and crash visibility
releases.summary: A patch with two user-facing fixes, both about a failure the user could see and the maintainer could not. A .md file double-clicked in Finder launched the app and then vanished: the bundle advertised CFBundleDocumentTypes so macOS routed the file, and nothing consumed it. It is now consumed on two paths, because there are two situations — at launch the file reaches Go before the webview exists, so App holds it until FrontendReady asks, and while running Go emits file:open for the frontend to listen for. The second fix corrects a belief rather than only a defect: the project recorded that no panic handler existed and that a crash therefore left nothing behind, which was true of this repo and false of the running program. Wails recovers panics inside bound-method dispatch, so the process survives one; it then returns an empty result that darwin/frontend.go passes to Frontend.Callback, whose JSON.parse throws before reaching the pending callback, and no call timeout is ever armed. The frontend's promise never settles and that operation is dead until restart, silently. App.reportPanic now records operation, message, stack and build version, shows a dialog naming the operation, and re-panics rather than recovering — swallowing during unwinding would return the method's zero values and report a failed save as a success. Coverage is pinned by two source-parsing gates because Wails binds by reflection and offers no seam to install it centrally.

releases.name: Repair from use and the standing defect backlog
releases.summary: The first release scoped from USING the packaged application rather than from review findings alone. v0.6.0's premortem carried one line a harness cannot close — install the DMG and use it — and closing it immediately returned a layout defect that five ABORT stations, the host gates and a 40-check screen walk had all passed over. This release carries that fix and clears the standing defect backlog: every open issue that is a defect rather than a roadmap milestone. Two of those defects were created by the v0.6.0 work itself — a UI route the contextual-bar removal took away, and a harness check that cannot fail — which is the argument for closing them here rather than carrying them further.

releases.name: Own the host, and make the editor editable
releases.summary: The release that removes the application framework and fixes the rule the editor exists to serve. Wails is gone from the running application: the window, the webview, the asset scheme, the native dialogs and the menu bar are AppKit and WebKit directly, behind hostPort, and a panicking bound call now REJECTS rather than leaving the frontend's await unsettled forever. Code blocks became editable in Formatted mode for the first time since syntax highlighting landed, and mermaid diagrams became editable at all. The cause was one undefined value: esm.sh resolves the bare specifier `codemirror` inside the vendored Crepe bundle to CodeMirror 5, which has no basicSetup, so EditorState.create threw inside the observer callback that upgrades a block, after the node view had set initialized = true, and never retried. Alongside that, the three editing surfaces were made to agree with each other, the floating contextual bar was removed in favour of controls on the blocks they act on, the ribbon stopped shipping the same command in two tabs, and continuous integration began compiling the code that actually ships.

releases.name: The application is named Dr. Markdown
releases.summary: A small patch with one user-facing fix and one cleanup, cut so the version the maintainer settles on carries neither. The application presented itself as 'dr-markdown' in two places, and neither was governed by CFBundleName or CFBundleDisplayName, which had said 'Dr. Markdown' for releases: the bundle FILE is what Finder, Launchpad and Spotlight show, and the EXECUTABLE is what AppKit puts in the application menu, taking the process name there. Both are corrected, and CI now asserts the bundle's filename matches CFBundleName because nothing compared them. The rename would normally strand the old install beside the new one under the same identifier; it does not, because installing replaces by identifier rather than by path as of 1.6.1 — a fix that landed one release before it was needed. Alongside it, a repository sweep removed two dead files and corrected three records that described a system which no longer exists.
